messages:
mike: quick heads-up — we need to validate staging rate-limit behavior after the burst-token refactor. planning a controlled traffic sim / soak. primary goals: confirm per-org and per-key quotas, ensure burst window behaves, and validate alerts/dashboards. who can help?

asha: I can lead the test plan. suggestion: two-phase run — 1) steady-state traffic to prime caches & kv, 2) burst storms to exercise token buckets. use k6 for steady and vegeta for short spikes. keep it in staging only, toggle new quota logic via feature flag.

samir: list the exact metrics we should watch + abort criteria. also we need per-key breakdown — some keys should be 'high priority' to verify bypass rules.

asha: metrics:
- Prometheus counters: `http_responses_total{code=~"4.."}` and specifically `http_responses_total{code="429"}`
- quota telemetry: `quota_acquire_requests_total`, `quota_rejects_total`, `burst_tokens_used_total`, `quota_tokens_available`
- latency: `request_duration_seconds_bucket` and `request_duration_seconds_sum`
- per-key/org labels: `org_id`, `api_key`
PromQL examples:
- 429s per org (1m): `sum by (org_id)(rate(http_responses_total{code="429"}[1m]))`
- burst tokens consumed (5m): `sum(rate(burst_tokens_used_total[5m]))`
Abort conditions: sustained 429 rate > 5% of total requests for 10m OR error rate spike > 10% for 5m.

rowan: can we surface a per-key 429 panel in Grafana during the run? I can add a temporary dashboard and share link. also add a panel for `quota_rejects_total` by route to catch any misroutes.

kelly: how do we control which keys hit new behavior? I want to run a gradual rollout: 10% of keys on quota-v2 for first wave, 100% for burst wave if things look good.

mike: yeah use the feature flag `quota.v2` in staging. we already have rollout tooling via `ffctl`. plan: 10% -> 30% -> 100% with 30m waits if metrics stable. for the spike stage, we'll explicitly route a subset of traffic to only v2 keys to stress the new code paths.

samir: traffic generation notes:
- steady: k6 ramp to target RPS with realistic token sizes and sequence lengths.
- spike: vegeta blast for short durations to test burst buckets.
- include a mix of calls: completions, embeddings, small prompts, long prompts.
Sample k6 JS to simulate mixed traffic:```js
import http from 'k6/http';
import { check, sleep } from 'k6';
export let options = { vus: 200, duration: '20m' };
export default function() {
  let payload = JSON.stringify({input: 'test prompt', max_tokens: 256});
  let headers = { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'Authorization': 'Bearer STAGING_KEY', 'X-Test-Quota': 'v2' };
  let res = http.post('https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', payload, { headers: headers });
  check(res, { 'status 200': (r) => r.status === 200 });
  sleep(Math.random() * 2);
}
```
vegeta command for spikes: `echo "GET https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" | vegeta attack -rate=1200 -duration=30s | vegeta report`

asha: important: set header `X-Test-Quota` on synthetic traffic so logs/filtering can clearly separate test traffic from other staging tests. also mark keys in keydb with `test=true`.

rowan: dashboard links (temp): https://grafana.internal/d/abcd/quota-run (I will add per-org 429, per-key rejects, burst tokens, and request latency panels).

kelly: who owns the runbook for aborting & postmortem? want to make sure SRE is paged if we see cross-service failures.

mike: runbook is `https://redwood.internal/runbooks/quota-staging-soak`. abort flow: 1) stop traffic generator 2) rollback FF `quota.v2` to 0% 3) drain staging route 4) open incident channel and ping eng-oncall. test owner responsible for taking action (asha for this run).

ci-bot: Deploy finished: `service/quota-staging` image `sha256:abc123` -> staging at 2024-09-18T15:43:10Z :white_check_mark:

asha: planning to run tomorrow 10:00 PST. timeline:
- 09:45: spin up dashboard and alerts, deploy traffic generator to runner nodes
- 10:00: start steady-phase (30m) with 10% keys on v2
- 10:35: review metrics, bump to 30% if green
- 11:10: spike-phase with vegeta (5x short spikes over 20m) targeting v2 keys heavily
- 11:40: cool-down and full-metrics dump

mike: tagging folks: @samir @rowan @kelly — please join the run and watch the dashboards. ssh access to runner hosts is in the runbook.

samir: small recommendation: emit a synthetic metric `test_traffic=true` label so alerts ignore the run unless we explicitly want to trigger them. we can temporarily mute production-like alerts for the run.

rowan: added temp dashboard and muted alert rule group `quota-staging` for the next 3h. link above updated.

kelly: I'll prepare the post-run checklist and eval prompts for Redwood Optimize to detect quality regressions between v1/v2. also will snapshot token usage by key.

asha: one more: watch for routing fallback behavior — if v2 service rejects, requests should fallback to v1 model variants per routing policy. include a smoke test verifying fallback within 1s.

mike: perfect. we'll meet in #eng-platform 09:50 PST for preflight. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
